brief.recommendation: Waiting would cost ~$274,712 in lost revenue (896s at $18,400/min) and exceeds the 60s degradation tolerance. Terminating the replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile, 4-min replay cost, may_interrupt policy, idempotent with checkpoint resume) releases locks immediately with minimal blast radius. Checkout is at 0% success vs 95% SLO.

audit.report: A replayable batch job (inventory_reconcile, pid 1314631) idled in transaction for 4.2s holding locks that blocked checkout, driving success to 0% (120/120 failed over 30s) with $18,400/min revenue at risk. After trade-off analysis showed waiting would cost ~$274,712 and 896s of downtime (far exceeding the 60s business tolerance), both guardians agreed in one round to terminate the batch job (4-minute replay cost, may_interrupt policy, idempotent with checkpoint resume). The pact was sealed but the authority denied execution due to a missing signed_provenance check, so the terminate action never ran. Total negotiation duration was 169.5s — nearly three times the 60s degradation window the business tolerates — and checkout remained at 0% success throughout. The blocker was never cleared; the business did not recover during this incident.
audit.root_cause: The replayable batch job inventory_reconcile (pid 1314631) idled in transaction holding locks that blocked checkout, and the authority's signed_provenance check prevented the agreed termination from executing.
lessons: For inventory_reconcile workload: Pre-register signed provenance for terminate actions so authority checks pass immediately — the 169.5s negotiation exceeded the 60s business tolerance because the authority blocked execution.
For inventory_reconcile workload: Add a lock timeout or statement timeout to prevent idle-in-transaction sessions from blocking checkout for more than 60s.
For inventory_reconcile workload: Ensure the batch worker emits heartbeat/progress signals so idle-in-transaction state is detected and acted on before 4.2s accumulates.
audit.negotiation_critique: The Database Guardian initially proposed waiting based on only 4.2s transaction age but missed that the job's typical runtime was 900s with ~896s remaining — the trade-off probe (step 13) corrected this. The Continuity Guardian accepted correctly. Neither guardian wasted rounds (1 round total), but the authority's signed_provenance failure made the negotiation moot.
follow_ups: Fix signed_provenance for terminate:batch_replayable_inventory so authority allows execution next time.
Add lock_timeout/statement_timeout to batch_worker role to auto-abort idle transactions.
Investigate why inventory_reconcile went idle in transaction (SELECT 1) — possible application bug.
